title: Multicenter, interventional prospective study to evaluate the efficiency of pre- and postoperative margin assessment of basal cell carcinomas using optical coherence tomography and line-field confocal optical coherence tomography during micrographically controlled surgery
summary:
Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common form of skin cancer. It often grows irregularly, which makes it difficult to remove completely during surgery. The current standard treatment is Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS), in which the tumor is removed step by step, with each step checked under the microscope. This method is highly effective but time-consuming and can be stressful for patients.

This study investigates whether a new imaging technique – line-field confocal optical coherence tomography (LC-OCT) – can help define the tumor margins more precisely before surgery. This could make surgery more efficient: fewer surgical steps, shorter duration, smaller scars, and still a complete tumor removal.

Patients with BCC will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

Standard group: Surgery performed in the usual way.
Intervention group: Before surgery, LC-OCT will be used to better identify and mark the tumor boundaries.

The study will compare, among other things, the number of surgical steps needed, the duration of the procedure, the amount of tissue removed, cosmetic outcomes, and patient satisfaction.
The trial will take place at five hospitals in Germany and include about 290 patients. Its goal is to make skin cancer treatment gentler, faster, and more efficient – while maintaining the same high level of safety.

interventions.name: Intervention group (LC-OCT): Preoperative tumor margin assessment using LC-OCT with targeted extension of the resection margins in case of tumor detection on imaging.
Control group (Standard MMS): Conventional clinical/dermatoscopic margin assessment, as routinely performed in clinical practice.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults (≥18 years) with BCC scheduled for MMS, confirmed by dermoscopy and histopathology or OCT. There are no restrictions regarding tumor size or BCC subtypes.
Exclusion criteria:
Poor LC-OCT image quality, incomplete adherence to the protocol, prior treatment of BCC. Anatomically difficult locations for LC-OCT are to be excluded (e.g., inner ear, medial canthus of the eye).
